title: Nightwatch field notes — Leo
content:
Nightwatch shift notes (18:00 - 06:00)
Owner: Leo Park (eng-sre)
Summary: quiet shift until a late surge ~02:12 triggered high tail latency for hosted-text-gen-v2 routes. Pager triggered, auto-fallback to smaller variant worked but increased error surface for a subset of requests.

Timeline / quick chronology:
- 01:58 — Routine infra deploy (infra/team-bastion) rolled out earlier but looked green. No alerts.
- 02:12 — Alert: route=hosted-text-gen-v2 p50->p99 latency spike (p99 ~ 3.2s; typical p99 ~ 0.95s). Alert fired: page SRE oncall.
- 02:13 — Joined #prod-incidents. Confirmed spike correlates with a small but high-QPS customer test (customer X staging traffic replayed accidentally into prod).
- 02:15 — Verification: metric shard shows increased seq length (avg seq_len 780 -> 2100 for bursts), resulting in slower kernel selection and KV-cache pressure.
- 02:17 — Applied quick mitigation: enabled route-level fallback policy to hosted-text-gen-v2-small for non-enterprise tier (config change). Traffic started to shift at 02:19.
- 02:30 — Observed error rate increase (5xx) on some sessions where tool-calling payloads exceeded small-model input size. Rolled back a portion of fallback to keep enterprise traffic pinned to original model.
- 03:05 — Incident declared: INC-4273 (owner: Leo Park). Priority: P2. Main risk: degraded quality and increased 5xx for long inputs.
- 03:40 — Collect logs and traces: trace ids collected and uploaded to S3 (path: s3://redwood-obs/incidents/INC-4273/raw-traces-20260321.gz). Added to ticket.
- 05:00 — System stabilized after customer throttling contact (CS routed to customer X to stop replay). Root cause confirmed: misconfigured replay job. Postmortem planned.

Commands / quick ops snippets used:
- curl -s "https://console.internal/api/routing?route=hosted-text-gen-v2" | jq
- kubectl -n inference set env deploy/route-router FALLBACK_POLICY=small:0.35  # temporary
- (/opt/tools/bin/trace-collector --ticket INC-4273 --out ./traces.tar.gz)

Immediate follow-ups (actionable) — runbook TODOs:
- [ ] Add guard in routing config to limit fallback for requests with content-length > 300k (owner: Leo) — due 2026-03-25
- [ ] Update runbook step for sequence-length spike: include quick knob to throttle replay jobs at LB (owner: Priya) — due 2026-03-24
- [ ] Create synthetic test to simulate long-sequence replay against hosted API (owner: Applied ML) — link to ticket SRE-842
- [ ] Add alert annotation to include seq_len distribution (owner: Observability team) — due 2026-03-27
- [ ] Add a regression test that ensures small-model fallback rejects payloads over X tokens instead of failing (owner: Serving-runtime) — due 2026-04-01

Notes to self / informal thoughts:
- The automated fallback is valuable — kept majority of traffic healthy — but the policy granularity is coarse. Need to extend policy to consider both customer tier AND request characteristics (seq_len, has_tools, streaming vs non-streaming).
- Kernel selection latency seems to blow up nonlinearly after ~1024 tokens on current optimized path; revisit quantization path for long sequences with infra team.
- Consider adding a short-circuit that returns a structured hint to client (HTTP 429 + suggest trim) instead of opaque 5xx for oversize inputs. This will improve UX and CS handling.

Communication / escalation log:
- 02:25 — Pager message: escalated to oncall escalation (Rafa).
- 02:28 — Notified CS lead (Maya) for customer comms.
- 02:35 — Slack thread pinned with traces + quick metrics summary.

Retrospective seeds (to refine during postmortem):
- Why did routing not account for replay job identity? (investigate tagging from ingestion pipeline)
- Can autoscaler detect and pre-warm kernels for sudden long-seq bursts? Might help with p99 tail.
- Are quota controls preventing graceful degradation for long requests? Check token counting path.

Attachments / artifacts I created during shift:
- traces: ./traces-INC-4273-20260321.tar.gz (in my home dir, uploaded link in ticket)
- quick dashboard: https://internal.grafana/redwood/d/seq-len/hosted-text-gen-v2?from=now-3h

Next steps (tomorrow morning):
- 09:00 — Sync with Priya and Applied ML to scope synthetic test (calendar invite sent)
- 10:30 — Start writing the postmortem draft (I'll structure with timeline, impact, root cause, corrective actions and follow-ups)
- Follow-up owners: add Jira subtasks under SRE-842 and link to INC-4273

Random TODOs (personal quick list):
- [ ] Move my runbook edits from draft branch into /contrib/runbooks (small PR)
- [ ] Cleanup my local traces dir (old traces >30d)

Closing note: felt smooth overall — automation and fallback saved us. Primary weakness: lack of request-profile aware routing policy. Documenting this now so we have a clear action list in the postmortem.

-- Leo
